fyNote: Financial year ends 31 December. 1H = January to June 2026 (unaudited). 2025 includes the airlines until December and a one-off RM11.3bn gain. Next results: Q3 2026, due late November 2026.

sources.title: Capital A quarterly report, half-year to 30 June 2026

segmentNote: Teleport and ADE now make over 70% of revenue (PR p.1).

how.title: How Capital A makes money now
how.text: Revenue = aircraft maintenance fees (ADE) + parcel and cargo delivery (Teleport) + travel bookings (MOVE) + licensing and rewards (Next) + food (Santan)

story.scale_label: logistics, engineering, travel app, digital and food

growth.profitNote: 1H2026 profit to shareholders was RM46m vs a loss on the same basis a year earlier; a % change is not meaningful.

items.label: Logistic expenses
items.tip: Trucking, air freight and last-mile delivery paid by Teleport.

items.label: Other operating costs
items.tip: Offices, marketing, IT and other running costs.

items.label: Staff costs
items.tip: Salaries for engineers, logistics and digital staff.

items.label: Consumables and fuel
items.tip: Aircraft parts and materials for maintenance, and fuel for freighters.

items.label: Finance costs
items.tip: Interest on borrowings and leases; lower after refinancing.

items.label: Depreciation
items.tip: Wear and tear on equipment, hangars and leased buildings.

items.label: Tax, FX and derivative losses
items.tip: Tax plus small currency and derivative losses.

items.label: Profit to shareholders
items.tip: What is left for shareholders: paid as dividends or kept to grow the business.

pnl.incomeNote: First half of 2026, after the airline sale: about RM2.94 of every RM100 ended as profit.

fiveYear.note: Only two comparable full years: earlier reports included the airlines. 2025 profit includes the one-off RM11.3bn gain. First half 2026: revenue RM1.58bn, profit RM46m.

rows.name: Teleport (logistics)
rows.tip: Air cargo and e-commerce parcels; revenue +21%, profitable for four quarters in a row.

rows.name: ADE (aircraft engineering)
rows.tip: Aircraft maintenance; revenue +19%, hangars booked through next year.

rows.name: AirAsia MOVE (travel app)
rows.tip: Flights, hotels and duty-free bookings; hurt by 11% fewer AirAsia seats.

rows.name: Santan (food)
rows.tip: Inflight and retail food; growing online sales.

segments.note: Net operating profit by business (PR). Teleport and ADE revenue from the quarterly report; others rounded from the release; segment sales include some sales between Capital A companies.

balance.note: The balance sheet shrank after the airline handover settled. Equity is RM548m after a 2026 capital reduction; borrowings of RM1.5bn are almost three times shareholders' funds, and short-term debts exceed short-term assets (Q2 p.3-4).

cash.wfNote: First half of 2026: the businesses Capital A now owns produced RM144m of operating cash, enough for equipment and leases, while it bought investment securities and refinanced debt.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM1.1 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Not meaningful: the last 12 months still include the one-off RM11.3bn gain from selling the airlines in December 2025. In the first half of 2026 alone, profit to shareholders was RM46m.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Not meaningful: the last 12 months still include the one-off RM11.3bn gain from selling the airlines in December 2025. In the first half of 2026 alone, profit to shareholders was RM46m.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (no cash dividend)
metrics.plain: No cash dividend. For FY2025 shareholders received AirAsia X shares instead (AR p.25).

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.9 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Not meaningful: equity was reset by the airline sale and a 2026 capital reduction; the last 12 months include the one-off gain.

metrics.label: Net margin 1H2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM2.94.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Company's like-for-like growth for 1H2026 (PR p.1). Reported revenue nearly doubled only because sales to the airlines used to be inside the group.

metrics.label: Profit growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Not comparable: 1H2025 included the airlines' profit.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM1.07 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 196% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Free cash flow 1H2026
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM91 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: Profit to shareholders 1H2026
metrics.plain: First half of 2026, after the airline sale: a second straight profitable quarter (Q2 p.2; PR p.1).

metrics.label: Net current liabilities
metrics.plain: Short-term debts exceed short-term assets by RM392m at June 2026 (Q2 p.3), so refinancing matters.

drivers.evidence: Capital A officially exited PN17 after the airline disposal (PR p.1)
drivers.why: Removes a major overhang on the shares.

drivers.evidence: Second consecutive profitable quarter; 1H2026 profit after tax RM50m (PR p.1)
drivers.why: Shows the smaller group can stand on its own.

drivers.evidence: ADE revenue +19%; hangar slots booked through next year; new 4-line hangar being built (PR p.2-3)
drivers.why: Its most profitable business has room to grow.

drivers.evidence: Revenue +21%; parcels +79% in 2Q2026; new routes to the Middle East, Europe and Oceania (PR p.2-4)
AirAsia cut capacity about 11%, hurting MOVE, AirAsia Next and Santan (PR p.1, p.4)
drivers.why: These businesses depend on airline passenger numbers.

drivers.evidence: Management calls conditions 'extremely challenging'; Q3 is a lean travel season (PR p.3)
drivers.why: Aims only to keep full-year results close to last year.

drivers.evidence: RM1.4bn owed by related parties at June 2026, down from RM5.1bn (Q2 p.3)
drivers.why: Depends on the airlines paying; management wants more third-party customers.

drivers.evidence: Borrowings RM1.52bn vs cash RM0.45bn and equity RM0.55bn; net current liabilities RM392m (Q2 p.3-4)
drivers.why: Refinancing and interest costs matter a lot for a small equity base.

drivers.evidence: Debt refinancing reduced interest expenses (PR p.1)
drivers.why: Each ringgit of interest saved goes straight to profit.

drivers.evidence: Net operating profit fell 21% partly because interest income from the airlines stopped (PR p.1)
drivers.why: Core profit rose 6% once this is adjusted for.

drivers.evidence: Clear mandate to expand third-party customers; MOVE's Wano B2B platform growing in China and India (PR p.2-3)
Share capital cut from RM8.8bn to RM0.58bn; net assets RM0.13 per share (Q2 p.4)
drivers.why: An accounting clean-up after years of losses.

drivers.evidence: P/E not meaningful; about 1.9 times book value at RM0.24 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: Investors are still judging the new, smaller group.

suppliers: Teleport ships through AirAsia and 55+ partner airlines plus its own freighters
Logistic expenses of RM465m in 1H2026: trucking, air freight and last-mile delivery
Consumables RM157m and fuel RM31m in 1H2026, mainly for ADE and freighters
Engineers, logistics, digital and food staff: RM355m in 1H2026
RM1.5bn of borrowings; recent refinancing lowered interest costs
customers: Main customer of ADE, Teleport, MOVE, AirAsia Next and Santan; RM1.4bn owed by related parties at June 2026
Maintenance at ADE; hangar slots booked through next year
16.3 million monthly app users; 37 million AirAsia Rewards members
Licensing the AirAsia brand into healthcare and hospitality
supply.note: Management's stated aim is to win more third-party customers and reduce reliance on the related airline group (PR p.3).

competitors.name: Grab, Traveloka, Agoda
competitors.how: Travel booking and super-apps competing with AirAsia MOVE
competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

competitors.name: DHL, J&T Express, Pos Malaysia
competitors.how: Parcel and cargo logistics competing with Teleport

outlook.text: A fresh start after the PN17 exit, with a clear mandate to expand and win third-party customers (PR p.3).
ADE booked through next year with a new hangar; Teleport opening new high-yield routes (PR p.3).
Aims to keep full-year results close to last year's; Q3 is a lean travel season (PR p.3).
Extremely challenging operating environment and ongoing geopolitical issues (PR p.3).

outlookOverall.text: Management says the group is heading in the right direction but expects a tough second half (PR p.3).
